claim: No total effective compiler maps every bounded-halting counter program M to an everywhere-correct binary-input poly(log n)-time checkpoint decider P_M, even though each M individually admits such a P_M.
status: PROVED/RESTRICTED proof uses Kleene recursion theorem; independent red-team review pending; computational finite controls
model: effective Turing program codes M; binary integer n; polylog(n)-time output programs on a fixed uniform RAM/ITM; effective C on all M
exact_quantifiers: not exists total computable C such that forall M, forall n>=1, P=C(M) is total, P(n)=1 iff M halts in <=n steps, and exists c_M,k_M finite forall n>=2 T_P(bin n)<=c_M(log(n)+1)^k_M
per_machine_existence: for every fixed M, if never halts P_M(n)=0; if halts in T steps P_M(n)=indicator[n>=T]; thus an O(log n) algorithm exists non-effectively
real_satisfiability_relation: instrument A_M with checkpoint bit H_M(length(x)) before a fixed correct P decider for 2SAT; SAT decider embedding conditional on SAT in P
